arguments.meaning: actor reference resolved by the native actor resolver
16-bit registered motion request stored at controller +0x66
positive float stored at controller +0x12c; non-positive values clear the field
positive float stored at controller +0x130; zero also clears +0x12c and negative values clear +0x130
positive float stored at controller +0x134; non-positive values select the native -1.0 default

sideEffects: requestSetterAddress clears controller status bit 1 when installing the request

registeredMotionResolution.indexRule: motion request N resolves to the one-based MOTION.BIN entry at zero-based index N - 1

evidenceBoundary: The handler, actor/controller resolution, request field writes, status-bit query, and one-based MOTION.BIN resolution are exact.

The general browser event interpreter must retain runtime actor arguments until their native dataflow is resolved. In the Hato functions, local constant propagation exactly resolves all three runtime-looking actor loads to AKIR.
The human-readable motion names come from the exact indexed MOTION.BIN entries and are not inferred from the Hato scene.
Hato's postlude exactly loops while status bit 1 is zero, but the engine-wide meaning of that bit (completion, interruption, or another terminal state) remains deliberately unnamed.
The native meaning of the auxiliary request floats remains deliberately unnamed.
